title: Localizing a quotient at a prime is the quotient of the localization
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, $q:R\to R/I$ the quotient map, $\bar{\mathfrak p}\subset R/I$ a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p=q^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak p})$, a prime ideal of $R$ containing $I$. Let $R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $(R/I)_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$ be the localizations at these primes [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $IR_{\mathfrak p}$ the ideal of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ generated by the elements $a/1$, $a\in I$. Then there is a unique ring isomorphism $R_{\mathfrak p}/IR_{\mathfrak p}\xrightarrow{\sim}(R/I)_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$ sending the class of $r/s$ ($r\in R$, $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$) to $q(r)/q(s)$. Equivalently, the ring map $\lambda:R_{\mathfrak p}\to(R/I)_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$, $r/s\mapsto q(r)/q(s)$, is well defined and surjective with kernel $IR_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient, line 1380): for a multiplicative set S of A, \bar S^{-1}(A/I) = S^{-1}A/S^{-1}I via x/s -> \bar x/\bar s; applied with S = R \ p, whose image in R/I is (R/I) \ \bar p since q is surjective and p = q^{-1}(\bar p).

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: the instance at Localization/Ideal.lean:391 with M = p.primeCompl, S = Localization.AtPrime p says R_p ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R R_p) is the localization of R ⧸ I at algebraMapSubmonoid (R ⧸ I) p.primeCompl = Submonoid.map q (q⁻¹ p̄).primeCompl, which equals p̄.primeCompl by Ideal.map_primeCompl_comap_of_surjective (Ideal/Maps.lean:514, f = Ideal.Quotient.mk I, surjective); IsLocalization.algEquiv (Localization/Basic.lean:172) then gives R_p ⧸ IR_p ≃ Localization.AtPrime p̄, and algEquiv_mk' (line 178) with the construction of the instance (of_surjective, mk' r s ↦ mk' (q r) (q s)) gives the formula.
